correctness.rationale: All quantifiers are fixed: n>=1 labelled worlds, >=2 named agents, each relation serial/transitive/Euclidean; each query is a freely chosen atomic valuation and returns the full-world one-step disagreement truth vector. Complement invariance and false endpoints give the 2^(n-1)-1 upper bound. The zero-vs-complement-pair constant-row KD45 models give a single distinct delta witness for every necessary pair, including against adaptivity. A two-agent local predicate is zero iff successors overlap; otherwise the two minimal positive sets recover exactly an unordered disjoint pair. Three-state inclusion-exclusion proves the quotient and fiber formulas. A standalone checker cross-checked all two-agent pointed profiles to n=7 and 50,001 multi-agent successor-vector cases, returning ALL_CHECKS_OK. The infinite family of finite n is proved symbolically; finite checks are not substituted for proof.

value.rationale: A natural observational task in multi-agent epistemic logic is to identify precisely what the group-disagreement connective can report, rather than inaccessible agent names and relational presentations. The theorem proves an exponential and adaptive-tight unavoidable experiment cost even under all-world feedback, while completely describing and counting the two-agent pointed quotient and its unidentifiable zero fiber. The sharp obstruction is realized by genuine KD45 models for every n; no arbitrary fixed-size slice, table repetition or unmotivated parameter substitution is involved. It exposes an experimentally relevant distinction between algebraic observability and physical relation identification, and an exact boundary for a specific recently axiomatized modality.
